variants.headline: Full shelves, empty household purses
variants.body: Food is for sale, but households cannot afford it and are going hungry beside full shelves. The gazette favours fair treatment of {target} rather than an adverse verdict founded upon assumption alone.

variants.headline: Food for sale beyond the buyer's means
variants.body: Households are hungry despite available food because they do not have the money to buy it. The gazette favours fair treatment of {target} rather than an adverse verdict founded upon assumption alone.

variants.headline: Hunger beside food that cannot be afforded
variants.body: There is food on the shelves, but people without enough money cannot obtain their meals. The gazette favours fair treatment of {target} rather than an adverse verdict founded upon assumption alone.
